Judi Dench is reflecting on her enduring love story with late husband Michael Williams
“Being with him anywhere would be enough,” the actress tells PEOPLE of Michael, who died in 2001
Dench writes about their great love in her new memoir Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It?
Judi Dench is looking back on her marriage to late husband Michael Williams. The acclaimed actress, 91, reflected on her life and career for a story in this week’s print issue, ahead of the publication of her new memoir Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It? — including the people who left their enduring mark on her life. One of those people was Michael, who Dench married in 1971. Looking back on his 2001 death was “the most challenging part” of writing the book, Dench tells PEOPLE. “I still miss him,” she says of the British actor. “Even now, 25 years on, I imagine he’s going to walk in through the front door.” When asked what she would do if she had one more day to spend with Michael, Dench says it’s “an impossible question to answer.”
“How could I see him for only one day, knowing that’s all I had?” she says. “Being with him anywhere would be enough — just to watch the tears roll down his face when he laughed.”
But in order for it to be a perfect day, she’d also want more of her family present. “My daughter and grandson would have to be there — the four of us together — maybe on one of our camping holidays in Scotland,” Dench adds. “But if I saw him again I wouldn’t be able to let him go.”
Dench also recalls a tender memory between Michael and actor Robin Williams , who appeared in Kenneth Branagh ‘s 1996 Hamlet film adaptation with Dench. Before Michael’s death, the couple visited actor Billy Connolly in Scotland and were staying at his home. “One evening there was a big party in the woods with a ceilidh and a bonfire,” Dench says. “Michael was very ill at the time and I could see him flagging, so we said our goodnights and began walking up this very steep hill.” “Robin Williams appeared beside us and offered to help, but Michael said he could manage,” the author and actress continues. “And Robin said, ‘Well, I think I’ll ride shotgun anyway’, which was such a lovely thing to say. I’ve often thought about that moment — Robin’s sensitivity and understanding, just offering to be there, gently supportive, without imposing himself.”
Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It? , due out from St. Martin’s Press, details Dench’s “heartfelt and hilarious” life journey, per its synopsis, from her award-winning career to her affinity for jokes and passion for the natural world.

Working with longtime collaborator Brendan O’Hea, with whom Dench also co-wrote her 2024 book Shakespeare: The Man Who Pays the Rent , was another rewarding part of the process, she says.
“When it’s just the two of us, there are no holds barred,” Dench says. Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It? will be published on Nov. 3 and is now available for preorder, wherever books are sold.
